descriptionChirho: An arachnid with a venomous sting, used literally for the desert creature and figuratively for instruments of harsh punishment (whips with barbed tips). Multilingual evidence is uniform: Spanish 'escorpiones,' Hindi 'बिच्छू' (bicchū), Arabic 'عَقَارِب' (ʿaqārib), Korean '전갈' (jeongal), Swahili 'nge' — all denoting the same zoological referent across all six occurrences, with grammatical variation only in prepositions and conjunctions.
